To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the combination of cells with different grid orientations and grid spacing is important for the reconstruction of the animal's location, (2) the relationship between grid size and subfield size is optimal for the reconstruction of location, and (3) the regular triangular patterns of grid cells are better suited to reconstruct location than any other regular tessellation of two-dimensional space and (4) that populations of grid cells are more accurate in predicting the location than equally-sized populations with place cells.

the grid cells of the medial entorhino-cortical (MEC) layer II can predict the position of an exploring animal more accurately than place cells of the CA1 region of the hippocampus, based on only a small number of cells and three grid parameters.

the grid cells of the medial entorhino-hippocampal system provide compact representations of the position of a moving animal that are more accurate than place cell representations, and that this is due to the unique spatial patterns of grid cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the key features of grid cells that allow for an optimal representation of the position of animals in the environment.
the analysis and simulation of the activity patterns of grid cells in the MEC.
the analysis and prediction of the spatial activity of MEC grid and hippocampal place cell populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the grid cells of the medial entorhinohippocampal system provide a unique and efficient representation of the animal's spatial position.
the grid cells of the MEC provide an accurate representation of the animal's location, which can be further used for spatial navigation.
MEC grid cells are the best candidates for providing the position signal to place cells in the hippocampus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MEC grid cells provide a unique spatial representation of the animal's environment and that the combination of grid cells with different properties is optimal for an accurate reconstruction.

grid cell representations of the environment provide a more efficient coding of space than place cells, and that the grid cell representations are more suitable to predict the animal position than place cell representations.
the MEC grid cells provide a unique and accurate representation of the animal's spatial position that can be subsequently integrated by hippocampal place fields.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regularity of the grid cells' activity patterns allows for an accurate prediction of the position of animals.
the grid cells of the MEC can be used to accurately predict the position of an organism in the environment.
grid cells provide a highly compact representation of the animal's location in space, and thus, the grid cell population may provide an efficient code for position representation.
